item.title: Advancing towards a Responsible and Resilient Digital Future
item.content:encoded:
Imon Chakraborty, Indian Institute of Technology Madras

Saji K. Mathew, Indian Institute of Technology Madras

Nargis Pervin, Indian Institute of Technology Madras

Viswanath Venkatesh, Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University

Digital technologies such as AI and platforms deliver significant value but also introduce serious challenges including bias, privacy violations, and workforce disruption. This special issue seeks research on information systems that are both responsible—fair, transparent, and accountable—and resilient—able to withstand disruptions and continue functioning effectively.

The special issue welcomes theoretically grounded research using various methods including conceptual work, surveys, experiments, case studies, and design science approaches. It seeks insights beyond simple adoption narratives, exploring post-adoption use, value realization, human-machine collaboration, AI governance, and long-term societal impacts.

The special issue is linked to the India Conference on Information Systems 2027 but is open to all authors. Submissions should challenge existing paradigms and clearly identify the specific technologies examined. Papers must have IS, behavioral, organizational, or societal contributions rather than purely technical focus.

Appel publié par Information Systems Frontiers. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Responsible AI and AI Governance

  • Human–AI Collaboration and Decision Making
  • Digital Transformation and Innovation
  • User Behaviour in Digital Environment
  • Digital Trust, Privacy, and Cybersecurity
  • Data Governance and AI-Enabled Decision Making

  • Design Science Research for Responsible and Resilient IS
  • AI and future of work and education
  • Opportunities and challenges of AI for society

item.title: Artificial Intelligence, Affective Computing and Video Analytics for Intelligent Information Systems
item.content:encoded:
Luigi Gallo, Pegaso University

Andrea Generosi, Pegaso University

Valerio De Luca, Pegaso University

Maura Mengoni, Marche Polytechnic University

Lucio Tommaso De Paolis, University of Salento

Josef Spjut, Nvidia

This special issue addresses the intersection of video analytics and affective computing in intelligent information systems. As video data expands across surveillance, social media, retail, and healthcare, advanced AI systems can extract emotional and social signals from visual content, enabling real-time understanding of user sentiment and intent.

The issue seeks research bridging computer vision and affective models to create human-centered systems for decision-making. Topics include multimodal approaches fusing visual, auditory, and textual data for emotion detection; scalable video processing architectures; streaming MLOps; and explainability techniques that address ethical and regulatory challenges in deploying affective video AI.

Submissions include original research and extended versions of papers from related conferences (CSEDU 2026, XR Salento 2026). All submissions are peer-reviewed according to Information Systems Frontiers standards.

Appel publié par Information Systems Frontiers. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Scalable video understanding
  • Emotion and sentiment analysis
  • Multimodal fusion
  • Streaming-native AI and MLOps
  • Video-language models for streaming
  • Real-time and distributed architectures
  • Explainability, fairness and compliance
  • Adaptive learning
  • Case studies and applications

Timeline

  • December 30, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Digital Technologies for Combating Unethical Labour Practices and Promoting Human Rights
item.content:encoded:
Stefan Gold, Technical University of Munich

Antoine Harfouche, Paris Nanterre University

Paul Jones, Swansea University

Maryam Lotfi, Cardiff University

Guoqing Zhao, Swansea University

Unethical labour practices affecting approximately 50 million people worldwide remain a critical social challenge. Digital technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and cloud computing offer potential solutions, yet research on their practical deployment remains limited. This special issue seeks contributions examining how these technologies can be leveraged for monitoring, detecting, reporting, and remediating unethical labour practices.

The call invites original, theory-driven research using various methodologies that provide nuanced insights into digital technology applications for addressing modern slavery, human trafficking, forced labour, and other severe labour practices. Priority is given to studies that challenge existing paradigms, explore underexamined dimensions, or offer innovative frameworks that yield both conceptual advances and practical implications for policymakers and practitioners.

Appel publié par Information Systems Frontiers. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Blockchain technology for labour monitoring
  • Artificial intelligence for detecting trafficking and slavery
  • Internet of Things and labour practices
  • Big data analytics for supply chain monitoring
  • Cloud computing applications
  • Worker voice technologies
  • Biometric recognition systems
  • Satellite imagery for labour monitoring
  • Machine learning for identifying at-risk populations
  • Digital technologies for survivor support and reintegration
  • Supply chain transparency and digital tracking
  • Modern slavery detection and prevention
  • Child labour monitoring
  • Forced labour identification
  • Human trafficking detection
  • Bonded labour practices
  • Digital solutions for labour compliance

  • Ethical and responsible digital transformation

item.title: From Adoption to Impact: Post-Adoption, Value Realization, and Societal Transformation of ICT and AI
item.content:encoded:
Jyoti Choudrie, University of Hertfordshire

Sherah Kurnia, The University of Melbourne

Gabrielle Peko, University of Auckland

David Sundaram, University of Auckland

This special issue addresses a critical gap in technology research by extending beyond initial adoption to examine how organizations and societies sustain, adapt, and derive value from ICTs and AI over time. While adoption decisions have received substantial scholarly attention, understanding post-adoption dynamics, continuance, value realization, and transformation remains insufficiently explored. The issue recognizes that technology adoption often fails to translate into expected organizational or societal benefits.

The special issue invites diverse research examining post-adoption phenomena across individual, organizational, and societal levels, including technology assimilation, transformation of work practices, and the complex risks and ethical challenges accompanying widespread ICT and AI deployment. Contributions should employ robust methodologies such as empirical studies, theoretical work, or design science research, addressing digital transformation, platform ecosystems, governance, algorithmic accountability, and sustainable technology practices.

Appel publié par Information Systems Frontiers. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Technology assimilation, routinization, and deep integration
  • Post-adoption behaviors: continued use, discontinuance, and switching
  • Value creation, capture, and measurement in ICT and AI use
  • Cross-cultural and comparative post-adoption studies
  • Changes to work practices, organizational structures, and decision-making
  • ICT-enabled institutional and governance transformation
  • Digital platforms, ecosystems, and network effects
  • Public sector and societal impacts of sustained technology use

  • Algorithmic bias, transparency, and accountability
  • Privacy, cybersecurity, and data governance challenges
  • Overuse, misuse, and unintended consequences of ICTs and AI

item.title: Keeping Humans in the Loop in the AI-Driven Future of Information Security
item.content:encoded:
Laura Amo, University at Buffalo, State University of New York

Richard Baskerville, Georgia State University

Rui Chen, Iowa State University

Matthew Hashim, University of Arizona

Yaojie (William) Li, University of New Orleans

Yuan Li, University of Tennessee at Knoxville

As artificial intelligence increasingly dominates both offensive and defensive cybersecurity, this special issue emphasizes maintaining human involvement in security systems and decision-making. While AI tools help detect threats and respond to attacks, they introduce new risks through generative AI-enabled phishing and behavioral manipulation. The issue seeks research balancing AI's role with human judgment and responsibility in information security.

Papers should explore how design science approaches create intelligent security artifacts enhancing human decision-making rather than replacing it, and how to mitigate human vulnerabilities while leveraging human strengths in AI-mediated security. Both established behavioral security topics and emerging issues related to AI risks and secure behavior in modern work environments are welcome.

Appel publié par Information Systems Frontiers. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Neurosecurity (NeuroIS) investigations of information security behavior
  • Design science treatments balancing security and privacy tradeoffs
  • Cybersecurity/privacy and AI/ML advancements intersection
  • AI-enabled security awareness, training, nudging, and behavioral interventions
  • Human-AI collaboration in security decision-making and response
  • Generative AI behavioral security implications: phishing, social engineering, insider threats
  • Intelligent security artifacts with behavioral implications
  • Adaptive and context-aware security interventions enabled by AI
  • Behavioral security theories in AI-mediated environments
  • Security behaviors in remote work, hybrid work, IoT, and cloud environments
